<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
\label{thm:gardam}
The torsion-free group
\begin{equation}\label{eq:presentation}
  \Gamma \;=\; \bigl\langle\, a, b \;\bigm|\;
    a b a^2 b^{-1} a^2 b^{-2},\;\;
    a b^3 a b^4 a^{-1} b \,\bigr\rangle
\end{equation}
does not have the unique-product property.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:up}
A group $G$ has \emph{unique products} if for all finite nonempty
$A, B \subseteq G$ there exists $x \in AB$ with exactly one representation
$x = ab$, $a \in A$, $b \in B$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
\label{ex:cert}
Take $u = aba^2$ and $v = b^{-1}$, with partner $u' = \varepsilon$, the empty
word, and $v' = b^2a^{-2}$. Then
$(uv)(u'v')^{-1} = aba^2b^{-1} \cdot a^2b^{-2} = r_1$, so the certificate is
the single triple $(w, i, e) = (\varepsilon, 1, +1)$: the relator $r_1$ itself,
with trivial conjugator. (The generated data number the relators from $0$.)
<!-- end example-1 -->
